notes: §1985:X.5.2.4 GR15: 'Called programs may contain CALL statements. However, a called program must not execute a CALL statement that directly or indirectly calls the calling program', and a CALL in a declarative 'cannot directly or indirectly reference any called program to which control has been transferred and which has not completed execution'. Both halves are a source requirement; ProgramTable.Activate refuses any CALL of a program whose activation count is nonzero and that is not RECURSIVE (EC-PROGRAM-RECURSIVE-CALL, the CALL is not successful, so ON OVERFLOW/ON EXCEPTION is taken through CallEmitter.EmitCallEcCatch, otherwise the run unit ends abnormally), and at 85 no program can be RECURSIVE because VersionConformancePass.VisitProgramIdAttributes refuses the 2002 attribute (COBOL0885). Probes: (b) SUBB calling active SUBA and MAINPG (ON EXCEPTION taken each time, nested calls then complete), SUBA calling itself without a handler (abnormal termination), PROGRAM-ID IS RECURSIVE refused; (e) a USE AFTER ERROR declarative entered after a failed OPEN (35) and a READ after it (47) calls the active SUBA (exception taken) and the inactive SUBC (runs). The witness (MAIN->SUBA->SUBB, no recursion) prints its five lines.

next.reason: 1985: "a called program must not execute a CALL statement that directly or indirectly calls the calling program."; 2023: "The program may be called while it is active and may call itself. If the RECURSIVE clause is not specified ... shall not be called". 1985 forbids calling any active program. 2023 allows it for programs with the RECURSIVE attribute; for others EC-PROGRAM-RECURSIVE-CALL is raised and the call fails.
